Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

substitute noun

a player who comes on for another

also sub, substitute player, reserve

classical

Mart. 5.24.8: Hermēs suppositīcius sibi ipsī, of a gladiator who is his own substitute (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 45

suppositīcius, suppositīciī m.

noun, second declension

Lewis & Short: “put in the place of another, substituted”; also “not genuine”, so in other contexts it can mean a changeling.

Other words

  • succēdāneus, succēdāneī m.

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Ep. 1.2.37: succīdāneum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 45

    Classically an adjective, “that supplies the place of something”; the noun is legal Latin (Dig.).

See also replace, team.

SourcesLewis & Short: suppositicius · Lewis & Short: succedaneus

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
